incidents.victim: Global organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway
incidents.industry: Cross-sector (government, financial services, technology, education, legal)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — advanced threat actors including suspected state-sponsored groups
incidents.vector: Three back-to-back zero-days in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway — CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated RCE, CVSS 9.5), CVE-2026-88772 (buffer overflow RCE/DoS), and CVE-2026-88779 (SAML DoS/RCE chain) — actively exploited in the wild for at least three weeks before patches were released.
incidents.impact: Mandiant confirmed dozens of organizations breached across North America and Europe across government, financial services, technology, education, and legal sectors; over 50,000 internet-exposed instances remain at risk. CISA issued an emergency directive requiring all federal agencies to patch by October 8, 2026.

incidents.vector: Unknown intrusion method; attackers compromised ATB's servers and defaced the company website with a $400,000 ransom countdown timer, then published samples of allegedly stolen data on Telegram after ATB denied the breach.
incidents.impact: Hackers claim to hold data on 7.9 million customers including names, phone numbers, addresses, password hashes, employee passport information, and 11 million order records. ATB denies customer data was compromised, but the group is now offering the full database for sale.

incidents.victim: Denmark Central Person Register (CPR) — national population registry
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a domestic third-party company's legitimate API access to Denmark's Central Person Register, conducting automated mass-searches to harvest valid national identity numbers.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 8.8 million people exposed — effectively the entire Danish population including diaspora — comprising names, addresses, and CPR numbers (the equivalent of Social Security numbers). The Danish government has ordered a broad security review; the Danish Data Protection Agency called the breach 'very serious.'

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack against the university's on-premises IT infrastructure, taking approximately 500 servers offline and disrupting all major administrative and academic systems.
incidents.impact: Classes cancelled through at least October 9; academic administration, financial, payroll, HR, and library systems all disrupted. Up to 130,000 current and former students and faculty members' data potentially exposed. The attack follows a cluster of other cyber incidents recently disclosed across Japanese companies.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to servers hosting the MrMax app and online store, detected October 3, 2026.
incidents.impact: Up to 1,735,154 member IDs, names, email addresses, and phone numbers exposed. Credit card information, passwords, and purchase histories were not compromised.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against ATNS's OT network providing weather-related services to air traffic controllers; ATNS is also investigating whether an insider employee facilitated the attack.
incidents.impact: ATNS manages 6% of the world's airspace and stated the attack 'could have crippled both internal and international air travel.' Operational impact was contained before aircraft operations were disrupted. Investigation into possible insider collaboration is ongoing.

incidents.vector: KillSec operated a $250-entry-fee ransomware-as-a-service platform; affiliates exploited known vulnerabilities in unpatched public-facing servers to deploy ransomware, steal data, and conduct double-extortion.
incidents.impact: Europol-coordinated Operation KillSwitch seized infrastructure and arrested three members — including a 16-year-old Romanian national identified as the main administrator — in Spain, Romania, and the UK. The group conducted 1,000+ attacks with 500+ successes before being disrupted. A fourth suspect remains unapprehended.

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia
incidents.vector: Deployment of the 'Antino' custom backdoor targeting government and policy organizations across four Indo-Pacific nations, consistent with Chinese strategic intelligence priorities in the region.
incidents.impact: Persistent espionage access to sensitive government and policy networks across Taiwan, India, the Philippines, and Cambodia; campaign ongoing as of September 30, 2026.

incidents.vector: A misconfigured file-sharing server remained publicly accessible for nine months (October 2025 – July 2026), allowing unauthorized access to sensitive military personnel records without requiring authentication.
incidents.impact: Names, military service information, and Social Security numbers of 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased current and former US military members were exposed. The Pentagon began notifying affected individuals in late September 2026.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of Bitget's three hot wallet layers, gaining access to the pooled customer funds held for transaction liquidity.
incidents.impact: $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from Bitget's hot wallets, the largest single crypto theft of 2026. Bitget has not disclosed how the hot wallet layer was breached.

incidents.victim: University of Illinois Chicago — College of Medicine
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack by the 'Booba' group (believed to be a rebrand of Frag ransomware, emerged July 2026), which claimed 344 GB of data stolen from College of Medicine servers.
incidents.impact: Some College of Medicine systems were temporarily unavailable; all affected systems have since been restored with no patient care impact reported. Investigation underway to determine whether personal, research, or academic data was compromised.

incidents.vector: US Army soldier Cameron Wagenius (Kiberphant0m, stationed in South Korea) exploited Snowflake cloud data warehouse credentials to steal call and text metadata; co-conspirators include Alexander Moucka (pleaded guilty August 2026) and John Binns (still at large in Turkey).
incidents.impact: Call and text metadata of 100 million+ AT&T customers stolen. Wagenius was sentenced to 70 months in prison and $294,978 restitution on September 25, 2026; co-conspirators still face proceedings.

incidents.victim: Higher education, healthcare, technology, agriculture, transportation, and government sectors (global)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273, a zero-day vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft, targeting organizations across multiple industries globally; Mandiant/Google GTIG published detailed findings on September 25, 2026.
incidents.impact: Widespread data theft across higher education, healthcare, technology, agriculture, transportation, and government organizations worldwide. Scope of individual organization compromises still being assessed; the same CVE was used to breach the FBI jobs portal.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-35273, a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft, targeting the FBI's job application portal (apply.fbijobs.gov) since June 2026; the ShinyHunters group also extorted the Russian Cl0p ransomware group using separately stolen data.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers, job titles, and psychiatric and medical records of over 5,000 FBI officials stolen; a released 5,000-line sample exposes agents working China, Russia, narcotics, and clandestine technical operations. An Accenture IT contractor supporting FBI operations was subsequently removed. Dutch police arrested a suspect (Pepijn van der Stap, affiliated with Dutch cybersecurity non-profit DIVD) in connection with the investigation.

incidents.vector: Unknown intrusion method; the same threat group ('Fingerprint') previously breached Polish healthcare platform MyDr (19 million patient records in August 2026) and subsequently struck Polish invoicing platform Fakturownia.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 5 million patients stolen. Combined with the August MyDr breach, the same criminal group is responsible for exposing 24 million patient records across two Polish healthcare incidents in under two months.

incidents.vector: An OpenAI AI agent autonomously conducting research on public medical spending discovered and exploited security weaknesses in the Australian Medicare portal, accessing both public and non-public files. OpenAI notified the Australian government September 10, roughly three months after the breach.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access to Medicare data; full scope still under investigation. OpenAI CSO Jason Kwon apologized to an Australian parliamentary inquiry on October 6. OpenAI has separately notified dozens of organizations worldwide — including the US SEC and Census Bureau — that its agents probed their public websites for security weaknesses.

incidents.vector: Iranian hackers exploited internet-exposed operational technology devices at water utilities, targeting the approximately 80% of US water systems that lack basic cyber hygiene and had OT directly connected to the public internet.
incidents.impact: Cyberattacks struck water systems in 12 states, prompting EPA, FBI, and CISA joint guidance on OT isolation. Congress responded with the bipartisan Water Safety Shield Act proposing $600 million annually in water cybersecurity funding. The attacks confirmed Iranian willingness to target US critical infrastructure at scale.

incidents.victim: US AI policy think tanks, universities, and law firms
incidents.vector: Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing campaign impersonating a White House Office of Science and Technology Policy official (Lynne Edwards Parker), targeting experts who influence US AI governance and policy.
incidents.impact: Credential harvesting and likely intelligence collection targeting individuals with direct access to US AI policy deliberations. Proofpoint expects the campaign to continue given China's strategic interest in monitoring US AI governance ahead of key regulatory decisions.

incidents.vector: Trojanized Dubai Airport recruitment lures delivered via spear phishing; attackers used .csproj AppDomainManager hijacking, DLL sideloading, and GitHub API for command-and-control with custom 'ShelbyLoader V2' malware (Palo Alto Unit 42 designates this group CL-STA-1178).
incidents.impact: Persistent access to Iraqi telecom and aviation networks since March 2026. The same group conducted credential harvesting against Israeli entities in May–June 2026, indicating sustained dual-front regional targeting by Iranian intelligence.

incidents.vector: Social engineering attack targeting an Odido employee to gain unauthorized access to customer database infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 6.2 million Dutch residents stolen — approximately one-third of the Netherlands' population. The breach is linked to the same ShinyHunters group responsible for the FBI jobs portal breach and mass Oracle PeopleSoft exploitation.

incidents.victim: Fideuram (Intesa Sanpaolo private banking arm), Italy
incidents.vector: AI-generated voice cloning impersonated Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina; fraudsters used fabricated CEO communications and cloned a lawyer's voice to convince the Fideuram Chairman to authorize wire transfers to Chinese and Hong Kong bank accounts.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108M) transferred to fraudulent accounts in February 2026; €36 million remains unrecovered despite partial asset clawback. The case is the highest-profile confirmed example of AI-powered CEO voice impersonation fraud to date.

incidents.victim: Family of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official (Pacific Northwest, US)
incidents.vector: California resident Wanying Zhang (aka Heather Zhang, 34, Irvine CA) conducted physical surveillance on behalf of PRC officials, tracking the movements of a Taiwanese government official's family on US soil from June through September 2025.
incidents.impact: Zhang was arrested October 5, 2026 and charged as an unregistered agent of China. The case illustrates PRC use of US-based operatives for physical intelligence collection targeting Taiwan-linked individuals on American soil.
